description: A big streamside maple 15-25 m tall with the largest leaves of any maple, often 30 cm across with five deep lobes, and a trunk often furred with moss and ferns. It shades the creeks and canyon bottoms of the foothills, turns yellow and gold in fall, and spins its paired winged seeds down to the water.

season_notes.winter: Bare grey limbs, green with moss after the rains, above the creek.
season_notes.spring: Long hanging clusters of yellow-green flowers open as the leaves unfold (March-April); bees and hummingbirds visit them.
season_notes.summer: Huge leaves make a deep, cool shade; pairs of hairy winged seeds hang in bunches.
season_notes.fall: Yellow to gold in October and November; the big leaves pile up along the creek.

notes: Big-leaf maple grows from British Columbia to southern California along streams and in moist canyons; in the Sierra foothills it is a riparian and canyon-bottom tree from about 300 m up into the mixed conifer forest, with white alder, bay, Oregon ash and dogwood. A tree 15-30 m (file 15-24 m, veteran to 30 m), dbh 0.5-1 m (radius_ratio 0.04), often several stems from one base where old stems died or were cut (stems [1, 3], veteran [2, 4]). Maples follow Rauh's model with opposite, decussate branching: rotation_deg 90 on both levels. Decurrent in the open (trunk.length_ratio 0.45, a fork in half of the trees), with a broad rounded crown of big lobes (photo W/H 0.6-1.05, base 0.05-0.19); in canyon forests taller and narrower. Bark grey-brown, shallowly ridged and furrowed on old trees, and in wet canyons covered with moss and licorice fern (bark lichen 0.7 as a stand-in; ferns are not drawn). Twigs green to red-brown, fairly stout. Leaves 15-30 cm (to 60 cm on shade sprouts), palmately five-lobed with deep sinuses, dark green above: leaf_shape lobed_large (new) with lobes 5, lobe_depth 0.6 and lobe_style palmate (lobes from the petiole, not along a midrib as in the oaks); big cards (cluster_m 1.6) and a lower leaf_fill since a few huge leaves make a spray. Photo summer colour linear r/g 0.88, b/g 0.50; fall yellow to gold, r/g 1.7. Deciduous: flowers in hanging yellow-green racemes 10-15 cm as or just before the leaves open in March-April (foliage.flowers, before_leaves true), leaves out by April, yellow in October-November, bare by December: leaf_on_by_month (new). Fruit paired samaras 3-6 cm with bristly seeds, hanging in clusters through summer and fall (not drawn: no suitable fruit form). Dead stems among living ones and standing dead maples are common in old riparian stands: deadwood and a 5% snag from the veteran.
